Where things stand
I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt — 333 tracked files, every one SHA-256 verified against its metadata (only export.sh differs, because the dump self-documents it in two places). Two things I found before writing any code:

Slice 33 is already in the tree, and it has not been run yet. The commit is 8c0772c "add claude changes", and docs/BUILD_PROGRESS.md carries the full Slice 33 section. But all three terminal logs are from Slice 32 — 1074 tests, 16 E2E scenarios, no Slice 33 numbers anywhere. So the tree currently holds one unverified slice. Worth knowing before a second one lands on top of it.

The next slice's work turned up three findings, and one of them blocks the plan's own next step. The plan says Stage 1b continues by emptying .chip and .visually-hidden from the remaining pages and extending SharedSelectorPrefixes to cover them in the same commit. I went to do exactly that and found:

F-65 — §11.12 names four kinds of control that carry the 44px target; app.css declares two of them at 36px. --touch-target is 2.75rem, and §11.12 says so of "buttons, links that act as buttons, checkbox rows, and the session links in the header". .session-link and .link-button both declare min-height: 2.25rem. Between them that is the sign-out control in the header of every page in both layouts, and the destructive action on four administration surfaces ("Revoke role", "Revoke display", "Take it off the menu"). The comment above .session-link says "they carry the §11.12 target height" and "Vertical padding rather than a min-height" — the declaration is a min-height, there is no vertical padding, and the height is 8px under. Both sentences are false about the three lines beneath them. Scenario 16 cannot see it: the reach selector covers a record row's action, a page-head action and a filter's submit, and none of those is ever a .link-button.

F-66 — the four detail surfaces are F-59's fifth copy. ManageMenuItem, ManagePerson, ManageTable and TableDisplays each declare their own inline copy of one .manage-* vocabulary — 20 duplicated rules — and where they overlap app.css they contradict it. .visually-hidden is the deprecated clip: rect(0,0,0,0) on all four, which is precisely the thing Slice 30 said it centralised in order to remove; the inline copy is later at equal specificity, so those four pages never got the clip-path version. .chip-warn is pinned to 
#fdecea/
#a3261c against the palette's 
#fbeaea/
#7f1d1d — a visibly different red on four screens. And five rules have drifted between copies (.manage-heading, .manage-rule, .manage-inline-form, and its input and select). The material half: .manage-inline-form input/select set padding: 0.45rem 0.6rem and no min-height and no font floor — so the one control each of those pages exists for is ~34px tall and will zoom an iPhone's viewport on focus and not zoom back.

F-67 — the gate that enforces "declared once" cannot tell a declaration from a comment. NoComponentRedeclaresTheSharedHandheldVocabulary substring-matches each prefix against the whole <style> block. It strips Razor comments and not CSS comments — while its sibling fact in the same file does strip them. KitchenBoard, CounterBoard and CounterSitting each mention .chip and .muted in a CSS comment explaining that those names are app.css's. So adding .chip and .muted to the prefix list, which Stage 1b requires, reports findings on three correct pages. The test already applies a "declared, not merely mentioned" standard — it just applies it to app.css and not to the components.

What I'd deliver, and one decision for you
Slice 34, as one archive: the shared .manage-* vocabulary lifted into app.css (keeping the name is safe here, unlike .admin-header, because every holder empties in the same commit); the two touch-target literals corrected and that comment rewritten; TableDisplays and ManageSitting converted, which empties StillExpectedToCarryRetiredTableVocabulary and turns it into an emptiness assertion; the three other manage pages' duplicate blocks deleted; the contract test's CSS-comment and declaration-position fix plus the extended prefix list plus a new fact for F-65; and scenario 16 extended to the detail surfaces it can reach.

The decision: scenario 16 can reach /administration/people/{id}, /administration/tables/{id} and /administration/tables/{id}/displays from identifiers the scenario already mints, and /administration/menu/{id} if CreateMenuItemAsync returns one. That takes the barrier from six surfaces to nine or ten and needs .manage-inline-form button in the reach selector. /administration/sittings/{id} stays unmeasured — a sitting needs a guest, a token and a join, which is scenario 3's arrangement — stated the way hidden-records already is. Say go and I'll build it that way; say index-only and the barrier stays at six and the four converted surfaces go unmeasured, which I'd record as an honest gap rather than pretend otherwise.

I have not written any files yet, so nothing to delete on your side from this turn.
